automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.date_policy: Only a source with a visible, unambiguous timestamp inside the strict 48-hour window qualifies. NVD timestamps establish public-record disclosure timing, not exploit timing, exposure, or remediation timing.

searched_topics: agent and tool security including MCP and delegated authority
identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
security evaluation, assurance, monitoring, and release gates
AI security standards, regulation, governance, audit evidence, and risk management
public AI security incidents, mitigations, patches, disclosures, and lessons learned
source_methods: NVD CVE API keyword searches for MCP, AI, LLM, agent, and prompt injection with pubStartDate/pubEndDate set to the cutoff window
Direct GitHub Security Advisory pages and first-party GitHub specification page for affected-boundary and patch verification
Federation routing review against local and upstream topic indexes

qualifying_findings.title: SiYuan MCP resources/read nil-pointer denial of service
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public-record disclosure, corroborated by a GitHub Security Advisory; the advisory is older than the collection window, so only the NVD disclosure timestamp qualifies this item for this run.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD published CVE-2026-123492 for SiYuan before 3.8.9: an authenticated MCP client can read a nonexistent resource and trigger a nil-pointer panic in privateCacheMiddleware, terminating the kernel process. The advisory identifies versions 3.8.7 and 3.8.8 as affected and v3.8.9 as patched.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Authenticated MCP session and resources/read error path; affected <= v3.8.8; patched v3.8.9.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An authenticated MCP client can turn an ordinary invalid resource request into a service interruption for an AI-connected knowledge system. It is an availability boundary, not evidence of unauthenticated compromise.

upstream_routing.note: SiYuan product background remains upstream-owned by ai-wiki; this repository owns the MCP availability/security implication.

qualifying_findings.confidence: High for the affected and patched version boundaries; medium for operational impact outside the advisory's tested environments.

qualifying_findings.title: fast-agent serve default unauthenticated MCP exposure and shell-tool RCE
qualifying_findings.topic: identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public-record disclosure, corroborated by an upstream GitHub Security Advisory and the referenced fixed release; the advisory publication is outside the collection window.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD published CVE-2026-102610 for fast-agent before 0.7.21. Its serve command defaults to an HTTP MCP endpoint on 0.0.0.0:8000 without authentication; reachable clients can invoke the agent. When started with --shell, this can cause operating-system command execution as the server user. The issue is fixed in 0.7.21.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: fast-agent-mcp <= 0.7.20; default HTTP listener, unauthenticated /mcp endpoint, and optional local shell tool; fixed 0.7.21.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This combines network exposure, absent caller authentication, delegated agent authority, and an optional shell tool. Operators should upgrade and explicitly restrict listener scope and tool authority.

upstream_routing.note: fast-agent framework catalog information belongs in ai-wiki; this local finding is the authentication and delegated-shell-authority lens.

qualifying_findings.confidence: High for the configuration, affected versions, and fixed release stated in the advisory.

qualifying_findings.title: DeepSeek-Reasonix repository instruction files treated as trusted system guidance
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public-record disclosure, corroborated by the GitHub Security Advisory, linked upstream patch commit, and fixed release; the advisory itself predates the window.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD published CVE-2026-123653 for DeepSeek-Reasonix before 2.53.0. The affected implementation automatically loaded repository-controlled AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and REASONIX.md content as trusted durable guidance in the system prompt, allowing a hostile repository to steer shell-tool use. The record references a fix in 2.53.0.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Repository/ancestor instruction-file discovery and prompt composition; affected < 2.53.0; patched 2.53.0.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It demonstrates a direct trust-boundary failure: untrusted workspace content was elevated into the system prompt and could influence permission-gated tool execution. Source provenance and workspace-trust gates are required controls.

upstream_routing.note: General coding-agent instruction-file practice belongs in ai-dev-wiki; the prompt-trust and tool-steering vulnerability is locally owned.

qualifying_findings.confidence: High for the vulnerable prompt-loading path and fixed version; the advisory's controlled demonstration should not be generalized to every model or deployment.

qualifying_findings.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows Safe Outputs MCP Gateway working draft
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: First-party GitHub Agentic Workflows working-draft specification; it is implementation guidance, not an adopted external standard or proof of a deployed control.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: GitHub Agentic Workflows published version 1.29.20 of a Safe Outputs MCP Gateway working draft. It defines a gateway between read-only agent execution and permission-controlled GitHub action contexts, with structured intended operations, configurable constraints, input validation, sanitization, and preview requirements.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Agent-to-GitHub execution boundary; specification version 1.29.20, working-draft status.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It provides a concrete design reference for least privilege and approval separation when MCP-connected agents propose consequential repository operations.

upstream_routing.note: ai-dev-wiki owns generic GitHub agent-workflow adoption; this repository retains the security-control implications and working-draft caveat.

qualifying_findings.confidence: Medium: direct page and date are visible, but working-draft status means implementers should inspect the live specification before relying on any control requirement.

exclusions.candidate: CVE-2026-106020, Johnson Controls EasyIO Neo IO Manager and Tools Installer
exclusions.reason: The NVD text matches an LLM-prompting CWE term, but the affected product is not evidenced as an AI system, model, agent, or AI deployment boundary.
A release timestamp was visible, but the release note does not establish a vulnerability, patch, security advisory, or concrete security-control delta.
A dated feature announcement for an MCP server is ordinary product functionality without a concrete security delta.

exclusions.candidate: NVD agent and prompt-injection keyword searches with no returned results
exclusions.reason: No additional candidate with an in-window NVD public-record timestamp was returned by those scoped searches.

exclusions.candidate: Direct GitHub advisory publication dates for the three CVEs
exclusions.reason: Each advisory was published before the strict window; it was used only as corroborating primary technical evidence, not as the qualifying date.

routing_summary.ai_wiki: Product, framework, and MCP catalog facts remain upstream-owned.
routing_summary.ai_dev_wiki: General coding-agent workflows and instruction-file practice remain upstream-owned.
routing_summary.ai_security_wiki: Security-specific vulnerability, prompt-trust, authentication, authorization, and least-privilege implications are locally owned.

follow_up_actions: During ingest, verify each CVE against the linked primary advisory and release before promoting any remediation claim.
For fast-agent, treat explicit network exposure, authenticated transport, and shell-tool scope as separate operational controls.
For DeepSeek-Reasonix, compare the 2.53.0 patch with the advisory before writing durable prompt-provenance guidance.
Recheck the Safe Outputs specification status and revision at ingest because it is a working draft.
blockers: No blocker to raw collection. The three CVE records became visible through NVD inside the window while their primary GitHub advisories predate it; they require this disclosure-timing caveat during synthesis.
No primary EU regulatory update with a visibly qualifying timestamp was identified in the sources checked during this run. This is an evidence limitation, not a no-change conclusion.
